statement:
You are given an integer array `nums` and a window size `k`. A window of exactly `k` consecutive elements starts at the left edge and slides right one position at a time until it reaches the right edge.

Return an array containing the **maximum value inside each window**, in the order the windows occur. There are `nums.length - k + 1` windows.

why.d: Checks negative numbers in `nums` and duplicate values in `nums`.
Checks a single-element `nums`.

hints: Recomputing each window's maximum costs O(n·k). Observe that an element is useless once a larger element appears to its right inside the window.
Maintain a deque of indices whose values are strictly decreasing from front to back.
For each new index, pop smaller values off the back, push the index, drop the front if it has left the window (`front ≤ i - k`), and once `i ≥ k - 1` record `nums[front]`.

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.description: For every window start, scan its k elements and take the minimum.

code.python:
def minSlidingWindow(nums, k):
    return [min(nums[i:i + k]) for i in range(len(nums) - k + 1)]
code.bash:
minSlidingWindow() {
    local -a nums result
    read -ra nums <<< "$1"
    local k="$2" i j lo
    for (( i = 0; i + k <= ${#nums[@]}; i++ )); do
        lo=${nums[i]}
        for (( j = i + 1; j < i + k; j++ )); do (( nums[j] < lo )) && lo=${nums[j]}; done
        result+=("$lo")
    done
    echo "${result[*]}"
}

solutions.name: Monotonic Increasing Deque (Optimal)
solutions.description: Keep a deque of indices whose values increase from front to back. A new value evicts every larger value from the back (they can never be a minimum again); the front leaves once it slides out of the window and is always the current minimum.

code.bash:
minSlidingWindow() {
    local -a nums result dq
    read -ra nums <<< "$1"
    local k="$2" i head=0  # dq[head..]: indices whose values increase front to back
    for (( i = 0; i < ${#nums[@]}; i++ )); do
        while (( ${#dq[@]} > head )) && (( nums[dq[-1]] >= nums[i] )); do unset 'dq[-1]'; done
        dq+=("$i")
        (( dq[head] <= i - k )) && (( head++ ))
        (( i >= k - 1 )) && result+=("${nums[dq[head]]}")
    done
    echo "${result[*]}"
}

solutions.description: For each window, scan its k values to find both the maximum and minimum and output their difference.

solutions.name: Two Monotonic Deques (Optimal)
solutions.description: Run a decreasing deque for the window maximum and an increasing deque for the window minimum side by side. Both fronts are read in O(1) per window, and every index enters and leaves each deque at most once.

code.bash:
windowRanges() {
    local -a nums result maxq minq
    read -ra nums <<< "$1"
    local k="$2" i mh=0 nh=0  # mh / nh: front of maxq / minq
    for (( i = 0; i < ${#nums[@]}; i++ )); do
        while (( ${#maxq[@]} > mh )) && (( nums[maxq[-1]] <= nums[i] )); do unset 'maxq[-1]'; done
        while (( ${#minq[@]} > nh )) && (( nums[minq[-1]] >= nums[i] )); do unset 'minq[-1]'; done
        maxq+=("$i"); minq+=("$i")
        (( maxq[mh] <= i - k )) && (( mh++ ))
        (( minq[nh] <= i - k )) && (( nh++ ))
        (( i >= k - 1 )) && result+=($(( nums[maxq[mh]] - nums[minq[nh]] )))
    done
    echo "${result[*]}"
}

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.description: From each start, extend the subarray while tracking its running max and min; stop as soon as max − min exceeds the limit, since longer extensions only widen the range.

solutions.name: Variable Window + Two Monotonic Deques (Optimal)
solutions.description: Grow the window to the right, maintaining a decreasing deque for its max and an increasing deque for its min. While max − min exceeds the limit, advance the left edge and drop deque fronts that fall out.

code.bash:
longestSubarray() {
    local -a nums maxq minq
    read -ra nums <<< "$1"
    local limit="$2" left=0 best=0 right mh=0 nh=0
    for (( right = 0; right < ${#nums[@]}; right++ )); do
        while (( ${#maxq[@]} > mh )) && (( nums[maxq[-1]] <= nums[right] )); do unset 'maxq[-1]'; done
        while (( ${#minq[@]} > nh )) && (( nums[minq[-1]] >= nums[right] )); do unset 'minq[-1]'; done
        maxq+=("$right"); minq+=("$right")
        # shrink from the left until max - min fits the limit
        while (( nums[maxq[mh]] - nums[minq[nh]] > limit )); do
            (( left++ ))
            (( maxq[mh] < left )) && (( mh++ ))
            (( minq[nh] < left )) && (( nh++ ))
        done
        (( right - left + 1 > best )) && best=$(( right - left + 1 ))
    done
    echo "$best"
}

solutions.name: Brute Force
solutions.description: Slide the window one step at a time and scan all k elements inside it to find the maximum.

code.bash:
maxSlidingWindow() {
    local -a nums res
    read -ra nums <<< "$1"
    local k="$2" i j hi
    for (( i = 0; i + k <= ${#nums[@]}; i++ )); do
        hi=${nums[i]}
        for (( j = i + 1; j < i + k; j++ )); do (( nums[j] > hi )) && hi=${nums[j]}; done
        res+=("$hi")
    done
    echo "${res[*]}"
}

solutions.name: Monotonic Deque (Optimal)
solutions.description: Keep a deque of indices whose values are decreasing; the front is always the window's maximum, and indices that slide out are dropped from the front.

code.bash:
maxSlidingWindow() {
    local -a nums res dq
    read -ra nums <<< "$1"
    local k="$2" i head=0  # dq[head..] holds indices, values decreasing front to back
    for (( i = 0; i < ${#nums[@]}; i++ )); do
        while (( ${#dq[@]} > head )) && (( nums[dq[-1]] <= nums[i] )); do unset 'dq[-1]'; done
        dq+=("$i")
        (( dq[head] <= i - k )) && (( head++ ))
        (( i >= k - 1 )) && res+=("${nums[dq[head]]}")
    done
    echo "${res[*]}"
}
